request.spec:
Show a due-total per calendar month: for every month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is
dated in, the due of the claims dated in that month that count.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show a due-total per calendar month: for every month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is
dated in, the due of the claims dated in that month that count.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

agent.result_text:
The sheet now shows a due-total for each calendar month, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**What it shows:** a "Monthly due" list placed just after the overdue panel. Every month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is dated in gets a row, earliest first, with its value in `month-<yyyy-mm>-due-total`.

**Which claims count:** a claim adds to its month only if it is OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED and isn't left out by the existing live-total rules (deferred, or open and dated inside a hold). That is the same set the sheet's other totals use. Each claim's due is worked out the way the claim rows already show it, so a settled claim keeps the figure fixed when it was settled. Claims whose due is n/a are skipped. A month whose only claims don't count (for example drafts or voided claims) still appears, with `0.00`.

**What changed:** this is a front-end-only change, worked out from the claim, people and rate data the screen already loads. No server, database or audit changes were needed and the tests don't expect any. There are two files:
- `features/rates/MonthTotals.tsx` (new)
- `features/rates/rates.slot.tsx` (adds it to the screen)

The type-check (`tsc`) reports two errors in `features/people/People.tsx`, which I didn't touch. They didn't stop the build or the tests.
